comment_text: Thanks for the video, a small caveat about your last point - live performances have been blurry for decades now (see: acousmatic sound). Electronic music performers exist in this weird realm where they interact with really complex music technology, but it is completely obscured from the audience and it's often impossible to tell whether it's just audio playback or if the sound is actually generated/controlled live. It's a slightly deeper problem that challenges just what is a "live music performance" exactly (you can argue it's just abstract theater, e.g. look at Genesis). At worst, you'd previously get slightly bored watching someone fiddle with their laptop, but now you can't even be sure if they've actually created the stuff you're hearing or not (also rapping to ai backing tracks etc.)
